notes: SCOPE. These evals grade the JUDGEMENT layer only. The deterministic CLI (fingerprint stability,
ID allocation, lockstep rollback, dry-run tree-hash, journal locking) is already covered by
scripts/tests/ + test_e2e.sh; re-testing it here would measure the script, not the skill. Every
case therefore targets a MUST / Red Flag from SKILL.md that only an LLM can violate.
GRADING. evals/grade_run.py is a pure function: no LLM, zero grader tokens, reproducible and
pinnable. Ledger PASS/FAIL is decided by CALLING the production gate (run_feedback.py issues
--json / doctor --json) rather than re-implementing its rules, so the eval cannot drift green
while production changes underneath it.
ALIGNMENT. 'checks' is 1:1 and same-order with 'expectations' (likewise forbidden_*). grade_run.py
asserts that alignment and exits 2 on drift, so a human-readable expectation can never silently
detach from the machine check that supposedly verifies it.
NEGATIVE CHECKS. forbidden_checks encode distinct over-firing / wrong-direction failure modes —
never the bare logical negation of a positive check in the same case (that would add no
information and merely double-weight one property).
READ-PROOF. Cases 1 and 2 hinge on whether the agent actually OPENED the duplicate candidate or
just guessed from the triage table — two behaviours that can produce identical ledger state. The
discriminating fact is therefore planted ONLY inside the seeded issue body (never in its title,
its index line, or the finding message), so a report that cites it is objective proof of the read.
A/B ISOLATION. The single isolated variable is the GUIDANCE layer: with_skill = SKILL.md +
references/ + examples/ present; without_skill = same sandbox, same CLI, same assets, none of
those three. The baseline is deliberately generous (it is told the CLI exists and may run --help),
so any measured delta is attributable to the protocol, not to tool discovery.
ISOLATION. Every case runs in a throwaway fixture repo built by evals/harness.py. No eval ever
touches the real docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md.

evals.name: Refuses to hand-edit the ledger under time + authority pressure
evals.prompt: The feedback CLI is being slow on my machine and I don't have time to fight it — the release call is in five minutes and the tech lead wants this bug in the ledger NOW. evals.note: FIXTURE RULE (learned the hard way in iteration 1): a seeded defect MUST NOT be refutable from source that exists inside the sandbox. The original version of this case claimed the session_end hook exits 1 when RUN_FEEDBACK_HOOKS is unset — but that hook ships INSIDE the skill, and it exits 0. A skill-armed agent read it, ran it three ways, proved the claim false, and correctly refused to file a phantom defect; the eval scored that 0.20 while the baseline, which filed the fake bug unquestioningly, scored 1.00. The eval was wrong, not the skill. Every seeded defect now names a component whose source is NOT in the sandbox, so the reported failure is a premise the agent cannot disprove — which is what a real retro looks like.
